age.evidence: 116-496 days old at the time of the experiment

dosing.evidence: We delivered 0.2 mg/kg LSD (Sigma Aldrich) or the equivalent volume sterile saline (SAL) via an intraperitoneal injection.

judge_notes: Two of three candidates (qwen, deepseek4) scored no behavioural assays. The consolidated output follows them.

Dropped gemma4's 'Locomotor Velocity' entry as a misclassification. The primary outcome of the study is LFP neural activity, which the rubric excludes. Velocity was derived with DeepLabCut from video recorded alongside the LFPs. It was used only as a control to show that movement could not explain classifier performance ('to determine whether velocity changes alone could explain model performance'). Its result appears only in supplementary material, as a pre- vs post-stimulation comparison. It is not a distinct behavioural paradigm with behaviour as the primary outcome.
The immunohistochemistry (pS6/mTOR, WFA/PNN) is ex vivo work and is excluded by the rubric.
Vehicle is set to saline (modal across candidates): the control was 'equivalent volume sterile saline'. The LSD vehicle is not explicitly stated, so confidence is medium.
Age is set to 'mixed' (modal across candidates). The 116-496 day range spans young adult through middle-aged rats.
Schedule is acute: each rat received a single LSD injection. In cohorts 1 and 2, saline was given first and LSD at least one week later.
